title: Ratios, rates and unit rates
lede: Comparing quantities, finding the better deal, and converting units without memorizing anything.

sections.md:
## Ratios
A **ratio** compares two amounts. If a fleet has 6 box trucks and 4 vans, the ratio of trucks to vans is 6:4, which simplifies to **3:2**. You simplify ratios the same way as fractions.

Careful with part vs whole. The ratio of trucks to **all vehicles** is 6:10, or 3:5, so trucks are 3/5 of the fleet.

## Rates and unit rates
A **rate** is a ratio of two different units: 300 miles per 5 hours, $18 for 4 pounds.

A **unit rate** is the amount for **one** of the second unit. Divide: 300 ÷ 5 = 60 miles per hour. $18 ÷ 4 = $4.50 per pound.

sections.title: Which deal is better?
sections.problem: Brand A: 3 lb for $7.47. Brand B: 5 lb for $11.95.

sections.md:
## Converting units
Multiply by a fraction equal to 1, arranged so the unit you don't want cancels. This is called **dimensional analysis**, and it's how scientists and engineers convert anything.

90 minutes × (1 hour / 60 minutes) = 1.5 hours. The minutes cancel because one is on top and one is on the bottom.

sections.title: Fuel for a run
sections.problem: A truck gets 6.5 miles per gallon. How many gallons for a 520-mile run?
steps: We want gallons, so put gallons on top: 520 miles × (1 gallon / 6.5 miles).

sections.label: Ratio tables
sections.md: When you scale a ratio up or down, multiply both parts by the same number. A recipe with 3 cups flour to 2 cups sugar becomes 9 to 6 if you triple it.

practice.q: A class has 14 boys and 16 girls. What fraction are boys?
practice.why: 14 out of 30 total = 7/15. Part-to-whole uses the total.
